title: Studying naturalistic human communication using dual-EEG and audio-visual recordings
author: Mazzini, Holler, et al.

steps.title: Arrange experiment room layout
steps.instruction: Define participant seating positions, ensure identical lighting, place two chairs on marked floor spots, add tables/counters for EEG equipment, set up visual occluder for the face‑to‑face occluded condition, and position a table with two stimuli stands for the referential communication task.

substeps.instruction: Mark chair locations on the floor with tape.
Place two chairs on the marked spots.
Add any additional tables or counters needed for EEG setup and supplies.
Prepare a visual occluder (e.g., a panel) and mark its floor position for the occluded condition.
Place a table between the chairs and put one stimuli stand on each side for the referential task.

steps.title: Assemble dual‑EEG hardware
steps.instruction: Connect the two 32‑channel ActiCAP snap caps and their control boxes to BrainAmp DC amplifiers, power packs, and the BrainProducts USB2 Adapter, then link the adapter to the recording and stimulation computers.

substeps.instruction: Connect each 32‑channel electrode set to its own ControlBox with a flat ribbon cable.
Insert separate reference and ground electrodes into the designated slots of each ControlBox.
Plug each ControlBox into a BrainAmp DC amplifier and attach a charged PowerPack to each amplifier.
Connect each amplifier to the USB2 Adapter via fiber‑optic cable (Participant A → Fiberoptic1, Participant B → Fiberoptic2).
If using 64‑channel caps per participant, repeat the above using the splitter‑box and additional amplifiers, connecting them to Fiberoptic3/4 as described.
Connect the USB2 Adapter to the recording computer with a USB cable and to the stimulation computer with an LTP cable.

steps.title: Set up audio‑visual recording
steps.instruction: Position cameras and microphones for the structured dialogue and referential communication tasks, using cameras with built‑in microphones (e.g., CANON HF G30).

substeps.instruction: Structured dialogue: place two cameras on small tables, one facing Participant A and one facing Participant B.
Referential task: place three cameras – front view of Participant A, front view of Participant B, and a side view capturing both participants.
Place one tabletop microphone in front of each participant, positioned to avoid obstructing view or gestural space.

steps.title: Configure auditory cue for structured dialogue
steps.instruction: Load the auditory cue into Presentation, connect a speaker (or tone generator) to the stimulation computer, and schedule a cue at the start of recording and every 60 s to mark turn‑taking.

steps.title: Configure cue and babble for referential task
steps.instruction: Use two audio mixers to combine multi‑talker babble with auditory cues and to embed the cue into the video‑audio streams while keeping babble out of the recordings.

substeps.instruction: First mixer (XENYX SO2): plug into power, connect stimulation computer LINE IN 2/3 (L + R), connect tone‑generator USB and LINE 4/5 (L), attach headphones via an audio‑splitter to the Phones output, set LEVEL 2/3 knob for babble volume and LEVEL 4/5 knob for cue volume.

Second mixer (ALESIS MULTIMIX4 USB FX): plug into power, connect microphones to MIC1 and MIC2, connect tone‑generator to LINE 3/4, route all camera audio inputs to the MAIN outputs, select external microphone input on each camera, adjust GAIN knobs for microphones, set knobs 1 & 2 for speech volume and knob 3/4 for cue volume.

steps.title: Prepare room for data collection (≈45 min)
steps.instruction: Power on computers and equipment, verify recordings, and launch software.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the recording computer and the stimulation computer.
Power on all cameras, insert SD cards, and confirm they record correctly.
Switch on the tabletop microphones and set the audio‑mixer volume to the desired level.
Check the condition order, speaker‑listener order, and position order for the dyad.
Open BrainVision Recorder, load the experiment workspace.
Open Presentation, disable network connection for precise timing, load the experiment file, and verify all settings.

steps.title: Prepare EEG supplies
steps.instruction: Gather gel, skin‑prep materials, cap sizes, batteries, and set impedance parameters in ActiCAP Control.

substeps.instruction: Fill two syringes with conductive gel and attach needles.
Collect NuPrep scrub, alcohol pads, electrode stickers, cotton pads, white tape, and a measuring tape.
Insert charged batteries into the two ControlBoxes and plug a PowerPack into each amplifier.
Connect one ControlBox to the recording computer via USB, open ActiCAP Control, select ‘Impedance check’, set ‘Good level’ threshold to 20 kΩ, and set timeout to 5 min.

steps.title: Meet participants and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Ensure phones are off, have participants read and sign the informed‑consent form, and answer any questions.

steps.title: Cap and electrode placement (per participant)
steps.instruction: Fit the EEG cap, place reference and ground electrodes, and reduce impedances to acceptable levels.

substeps.instruction: Reference electrodes: clean skin on left and right mastoids (or TP9/TP10), dry, attach sticker, fill with gel, and insert.
Measure head circumference from nasion to inion; choose appropriate ActiCAP size (e.g., 54 cm, 56 cm, 58 cm, 60 cm).
Place the cap, secure the chin strap, and center it so Cz lies midway between nasion‑inion and ear‑tops.
Insert all cap electrodes into the green holders.
Connect the cap cable and reference/ground cables to the participant’s ControlBox.

Impedance reduction: start with reference and ground electrodes, fill with gel, click the ‘Z’ symbol on the ControlBox (or in BrainVision Recorder) and distribute gel until the electrode light turns green (≤20 kΩ for active electrodes, ≤5 kΩ for passive). Repeat for every electrode, then stop the impedance check.

steps.title: Place EOG and EMG electrodes
steps.instruction: Add eye‑movement and mouth‑movement electrodes as required by the task.

substeps.instruction: Structured dialogue (EOG): clean skin above and below one eye and at the outer canthi of both eyes, dry, attach electrodes with stickers, fill with gel, and achieve target impedance.

Referential communication (EMG): clean skin near the superior and inferior orbicularis oris muscles on the same side of the mouth, place a third electrode on the right cheek, attach stickers, fill with gel, and reduce impedances as above.

steps.title: Start recording
steps.instruction: Power the amplifiers, verify signal quality, equip participants with headphones (referential task), and confirm camera views.

substeps.instruction: Switch on both amplifiers and connect their cables to the respective ControlBoxes.
Ask participants to stay steady, click the signal icon in BrainVision to display EEG traces, and confirm a clear, unperturbed signal.
For the referential task, place headphones over each participant’s EEG cap.
Check that Camera A records Participant A, Camera B records Participant B, and the side camera captures both.

description: In the last two decades, a multitude of studies in the field of cognitive neuroscience started to investigate social interaction and the cognitive processes behind it.1,2 Up until then, most research was limited to the study of the brain of a single participant involved in social interaction, therefore not capturing the dyadic or group aspect of social interaction.3 The advent of hyperscanning techniques, such as dual-electroencephalography (EEG), offered the possibility to measure the brain activity of multiple individuals at the same time, enabling the investigation of the neural dynamics beyond a single participant and between interacting brains.4,5,6,7,8 Due to its high temporal resolution, collecting dual-EEG in combination with audio-visual data also offers the opportunity to directly relate the behavioral and neural aspects of social interaction to each other. This protocol describes the necessary steps for collecting dual-EEG and audio-visual data to study human face-to-face communication, as well as its underlying intra- and inter-brain neural dynamics. The collected data will be suitable for different types of analyses, such as conversation and gesture analyses, intra-brain spectral and time-frequency analyses, as well as intra- and inter-brain connectivity and coherence analyses. More specifically, we describe the setup and procedure implemented in two experiments, to illustrate how the protocol can be expanded to address multiple research questions on human communication. We first refer to the study by Drijvers & Holler,9 one of the first dual-EEG studies of multimodal face-to-face interaction. The authors investigated the influence of spatial orientation and the visibility of bodily signals on intra- and inter-brain neural synchrony during dyadic interactions.
